summary: Opened the one in-model consequence of the v3.7.0 read-index rewrite that I had previously noted but left unclaimed. New investigation @read_retry_growth: readOnly.addRequest appends unconditionally without the context-keyed deduplication v3.6.0 used, and every admitted MsgReadIndex broadcasts a heartbeat, while entries leave unconfirmedReads only when a quorum ack position advances maybeAdvance - so N same-context retries (which the node contract at node.go:222-223 tells callers to make) produce N entries and N broadcasts. Recorded it as a sourced behavior fact plus an open necessary gap asking what bounds same-context outstanding retries and whether checkQuorum guarantees step-down first. The interpretation is source-only, unresolved (defect claim unresolved, not asserted), with explicit reasons: a caller retrying forever recreates its own obligation, nonprogress without quorum is correct behavior, healthy quorums confirm on the next heartbeat response, and the rewrite's changelog frames the removal as the stale-read-index fix - so a bounded-consequence argument is still missing. This thread is independent of the earlier refuted ack-validation thread.
